title: Smaller Than a Virus? Viroids Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A potato grows long and thin like a spindle, and a cow stumbles and cannot stand. The cause is not a virus, but something even simpler. Diya stops at this line in her notes: something with no protein coat, or with no nucleic acid at all, can still cause disease?

We start from a virus and take parts away. A live zoom ladder goes from a sick potato plant to a spindle-shaped tuber, a tuber cell and one viroid: free RNA of low molecular weight with no protein coat (T. O. Diener, 1971, potato spindle tuber disease). Then prions step by step: an abnormally folded protein that makes normal proteins misfold in a chain reaction and damages nerve cells (BSE or mad cow disease in cattle, CJD in humans). Virus vs viroid vs prion side by side, a worked classification key, the exam trap on molecular weight, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 19 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
